summary: Lookout on Keystone Peak, Mineral County, MT, in use 1934 to 1980; sources disagree on whether it was destroyed or removed. No site description found.

facts.status_note: Sources disagree on how it ended: firelookout.com says destroyed in 1980, Montanalookouts says removed with no date.

events.note: firelookout.com dates the tower to 1934; the Montana History Portal gives 1934 as the start of lookout use on the peak
firelookout.com says destroyed in 1980; the Montana History Portal says the lookout stood until 1980; Montanalookouts lists it as removed, undated

evidence.supports: peak, creek and town named for the Keystone Mine, discovered by Phillip O'Rourke and others in 1887
evidence.quote: named for the Keystone Mine, discovered and developed by Phillip O’Rourke and others in 1887

evidence.supports: silver mine ran on and off until the 1930s
evidence.quote: The silver mine operated sporadically until the 1930s.

evidence.supports: a fire lookout stood on the peak from 1934 until 1980
evidence.quote: There was a fire lookout on the peak from 1934 until 1980

evidence.supports: tower dated 1934, described as a 10' pole L-4 tower
firelookout.com gives peak elevation 5878 ft, against 5843 ft from the Montana History Portal
Lolo National Forest listed as agency
Lolo National Forest listed as agency
Montanalookouts lists the tower as removed, no date
Forest Fire Lookout Association list marks the tower gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com says destroyed in 1980; Montanalookouts says removed with no date. Neither source is more specific, so the story reports both and does not choose between them.
Montana History Portal gives 5843 ft; firelookout.com gives 5878 ft. The story reports the Portal figure and notes the firelookout.com figure.

notes_for_editor: Brief checked: status gone, kind tower and Lolo National Forest agree with the sources; no corrections. The 1934 build date rests on firelookout.com and is consistent with the Montana History Portal's 1934 start. The fate is disputed (destroyed in 1980 vs removed, undated) and the story says so. No staffing, fire, access or site-condition source was found. Not tried: Lolo NF records, Montana SHPO files, a photo search for the summit.
